text:
ana: Quick async standup — API gateway / routing / auth / rate limits (what I did / blockers / today)
ana: Done: merged routing + auth adapter PR (ref #5292), kicked off 5% canary for the new throttling policy. basic smoke looked good.
ana: Blocker: thin-client replay shows ~0.5% 429s coming from edge nodes, not sure if token-bucket sizing should be bumped for short bursts.
ana: Today: plan to scale token bucket on edge pool, add a canary rollback script, and follow up on the CR comments.
liam: saw the spike on the dashboard at ~09:12 UTC, can you drop the replay logs? i ran local replay and didn't repro.
ana: log snippet from the replay (trimmed):
```
[2024-03-12T09:12:08Z] edge-node-12 auth: token_refill=50ms bucket_tokens=3 req=GET /v1/generate -> 429
[2024-03-12T09:12:08Z] edge-node-12 rate: route=thin-client short_burst=5 allowed=3
```
liam: hmm looks like bursts are higher than the refill window during our thin-client test. could be traffic shaping mismatch.
sophie: left CR comments on #5292 about an off-by-one in the bucket refill math — could produce exactly this symptom. :mag:
morgan: can we gate the change behind a feature flag so we can flip fast if it misbehaves? also add a metric for "burst_denied" to the dashboard.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary throttle-change (dc-rl-042) — build 2024.03.12-abc123 — targets: 5% edge nodes
oncall: watching the canary. if 429s exceed 1% for 10m, revert and @morgan will open the rollback.
ana: agreed — i'll push a small change to bump bucket_tokens by +2 for thin-client routes and add the feature flag.
liam: quick question on routing: should internal admin traffic bypass rate limits entirely? (we have some health probes that hit admin endpoints)
sophie: yes — add header `X-Internal: true` and short-circuit limiter for routes with `allow_internal: true`. i can add a quick policy snippet.
nana: sample routing rule i'll add:```
- route: /admin/*
  match_headers:
    X-Internal: true
  rate_limit:
    enabled: false
  auth: required
```
morgan: CR ping @sophie — can you re-approve after i add unit tests for the negative refill case? also add a small integration test that replays thin-client traffic.
sophie: will review in the next hour, should be quick. :thumbsup:
nana: tagging SLO owners — @oncall if you want a rollback window or different threshold, say now.
oncall: keep the 1%/10m threshold for now, i'll escalate if noise increases.
liam: FYI i added a small dashboard panel comparing pre/post canary 429 rate per edge region. sharing link in #eng-metrics.
nana: thanks — i'll update the PR with the feature-flag and the extra tests, then merge if green.
morgan: will be available for emergency rollback and can cut a hotfix release if needed.
sophie: good plan.
nana: ok signing off for now — will post another quick update after the next canary eval. :wave:
